cells.tense: Right now the whole thing is visible and you are the one holding the pen.
cells.ask: Write the shape of the whole thing on one page — not the parts, the pattern — and hand it to someone who was in it with you.
cells.core:
You can stand far enough back to see how the pieces fit and still stay inside the thing you're looking at, close to it and over it at once. That's not common. People bring you the mess, and you don't flinch or flatten it — you show them the shape it already has, and they can use what you show them.
This is going well when the pattern arrives on its own and you let it land before you do anything with it. Then you take the whole picture and start working it, letting the pattern do some of the labor instead of leaving it as something only you can see. That step demands the comfort of watching from a distance — the sight is only one half.
cells.sheetLine: You see the whole shape and can stand inside it.
cells.verb: seeing the whole pattern at once, nothing hidden
cells.place: where the pattern shows itself whole while you stand inside it

cells.tense: You are leaning into a final version of the picture before the last pieces have arrived.
cells.ask: Say the pattern out loud as unfinished — leave the one part you can't see yet unnamed, and stop there.
cells.core:
You want the whole thing now. So you reach past what's actually in front of you to the finished version, the one where every piece has landed and nothing is left open. That reach runs ahead of the material. You start calling the pattern done before it is, and your view narrows to fit the conclusion you already have.
The lack here isn't more insight. It's being at the beginning again — open, not yet pointed, before the pattern catches fire. The picture you're forcing closed has a part still arriving, and you can't make it out while you hold the lid down.
cells.sheetLine: You're finishing the pattern before it's done arriving.
cells.verb: seeing the whole pattern at once, nothing hidden
cells.place: where the pattern shows itself whole while you stand inside it

cells.tense: You saw something whole once, and you are still at the door of that room.
cells.ask: Pick one small piece of what you already understand and give it physical form today — a written line, a sketch, a set of steps.
cells.core:
You know how to see the whole thing. What stopped is the step from seeing to form. The pattern was clear and nothing came of it, and since then you've kept the sight private — watching, not shaping. There's no lack of understanding here. The understanding just isn't landing anywhere it could be used, and waiting for a better moment keeps it that way.
What pulls you back is naming one piece and giving it a shape you can hold. Not all of it — one corner, made real. Choosing which piece is yours to choose, and making that choice is what gets you through the door you've been standing at.
cells.sheetLine: You can see it. You've stopped giving it a shape.

cells.tense: The perceiving is already running and you are not claiming it as yours.
cells.ask: Name one moment today where you saw how something fit, and say 'I saw that' — to yourself or out loud.
cells.core:
You walk into a room and its shape arrives — who holds what, where the tension sits, what's about to happen. It comes fast and it's usually right. You call it just noticing, or reading the room, or common sense, and you move on. The perceiving runs whenever you're with people, and nobody has signed for it, including you.
When it's going well here, you catch what's arriving as it comes — a look, a shift, a piece you didn't have before — and you let yourself be the one meeting it. That's the same act as seeing the whole pattern, before it gets named. Signing for it is the move you haven't made.
cells.sheetLine: You see it, and you haven't said it's yours.
